reference.title: Cable Lying Triceps Extension
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read and the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the bar lowers toward the head, breathe out as you straighten the arms.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, short pause, about 1.4 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lower with the upper arms still and the bar under control above the head.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; slower lowering

cues.text: Lie on a flat bench with the head toward a low pulley, feet flat; hold the straight bar overhand about shoulder width, arms straight over the upper chest and angled slightly back toward the head.
Breathe in and bend only the elbows, lowering the bar in an arc toward the top of the head.
Stop with the bar just above and behind the forehead, elbows pointing up and not flaring.
Breathe out and straighten the elbows back to the start; the upper arms stay still.
Pause with the arms straight but not locked hard; keep tension on the cable.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arms swinging toward the feet (turning it into a pullover-press)
mistakes.fix: Fix the upper arms slightly back toward the head and move only the forearms.
Keep the elbows about shoulder width, pointing up.

mistakes.mistake: Lowering the bar onto the face
mistakes.fix: Aim for just above and behind the forehead; control the stack.
Keep the head, upper back and buttocks on the pad, feet planted.

kinematics.norm: From nearly straight to about 100-120 degrees with the bar behind the forehead (clinical opinion); activation and relative force were matched across the three heads at 90 degrees of flexion or more (PLoS ONE 2021)
Slightly past vertical toward the head and still; at 90 degrees of shoulder flexion and above the medial head carried the most force (Kholinne 2018)
Overhand about shoulder width on a straight bar (clinical opinion)
Low pulley behind the head so the cable pulls along the forearms through the range (clinical opinion)
Head, upper back and buttocks on the bench, feet flat on the floor (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s lowering and 1-1.5 s pressing (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Lying Triceps Extension, video (movement reference)

Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, ACE-sponsored; 15 women, 8 exercises at 70% 1RM)

The different role of each head of the triceps brachii muscle in elbow extension (Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2018;52(3):201-205; PubMed 29503079; EMG plus OpenSim at 0-180 degrees of shoulder elevation)
Effect of elbow joint angles on electromyographic activity versus force relationships of synergistic muscles of the triceps brachii (PLoS ONE 2021; PMC8174684)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain in the elbow or shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lower under control; the bar travels above the face.
Get into position holding the bar on the chest (or have a partner pass it), and at the end of the set return it to the chest before sitting up so the stack lowers gently.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Elbow pain: use a rope or an angled bar and a shorter range (clinical opinion).
Shoulder discomfort: keep the upper arms vertical rather than angled back.
regressions: Dumbbell skull crusher with light dumbbells.
progressions: Overhead cable triceps extension (more triceps growth than the arm-at-the-side position in a 12-week study, PubMed 35819335).

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Prime mover: straightens the elbow against the cable. With the shoulder flexed past 90 degrees the long head works from a lengthened position (Kholinne 2018 measured head roles across shoulder elevation).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Prime mover: straightens the elbow against the cable. With the shoulder flexed past 90 degrees the long head works from a lengthened position (Kholinne 2018 measured head roles across shoulder elevation).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Hold the upper arm angled back as the cable pulls it toward the head.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Hold the upper arm angled back as the cable pulls it toward the head.
muscleNotes.pec_r: Steadies the upper arm against the cable's pull toward the head.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Steadies the upper arm against the cable's pull toward the head.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the back flat on the bench.
